nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of precursor
nodes.procedure: A homogeneous solution was formed by mixing RuCl3, boric acid (H3BO3) and GO solution using deionized water as the solvent, which was then reacted in a Teflon autoclave at 180°C for 12 h to obtain the precursor sample.

nodes.name: Sintering of precursor
nodes.procedure: The precursor sample was further sintered at 500°C for 2 h in an H2/Ar atmosphere to obtain the RuC-B-O/rGO complex.

nodes.description: HER performance in 1 M KOH using three-electrode system
nodes.source_text: The HER performance of various electrocatalysts... was measured with a typical three-electrode system at 25°C... The overpotential of the Ru_C - B - O / rGO catalyst was only 12 mV at -10 mA cm^{-2}... Tafel slope of Ru_C - B - O / rGO is only 31.5 mV dec^{-1}... overpotentials of Ru_C - B - O / rGO are 12, 35, and 52 mV at... -10, -50, and -100 mA cm^{-2}... limiting current density of Ru_C - B - O / rGO can reach -1524.3 mA cm^{-2} with 90% iR correction

nodes.description: AEMWE device performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The AEMWE device based on Ru_C - B - O / rGO only requires 1.73 V to reach an industrial current density of -1 A cm^{-2} at the temperature of 80 °C... the precious metal loading in the AEMWE device is only 0.1 mg cm^{-2}... the cell voltage of the Ru_C - B - O / rGO -based electrolyzer can remain stable for more than 120 h and the degradation rate is only 0.15 mV h^{-1} at the large current density of -1 A cm^{-2}

nodes.characterization_summary: Fine Ru clusters distributed on B-O/rGO surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscope (TEM) image reveals that fine clusters are distributed on the B-O/rGO surface (Figure S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern analysis indicates precursor exhibits low crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern analysis indicates that the precursor exhibits low crystallinity (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of Ru_C - B - O/rGO is 339.9 m² g⁻¹ with average pore size ~1.2 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of the Ru_C - B - O/rGO compound was 339.9 m² g⁻¹ with an average pore size of ~1.2 nm (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: ~2.2 nm Ru_C grown uniformly on B-O/rGO support and mainly exposes (101) crystal plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and TEM images revealed that the ~2.2 nm Ru_C was grown on the B-O/rGO support uniformly (Figures 1b and S4a,b).

properties.description: High-resolution image showing bright central feature with 1 nm scale bar
properties.label: Top-left panel

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS mapping shows positions of B/O elements and Ru elements partially overlap, indicating successful B/O coordination with Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping of Ru_C - B - O /rGO show that the positions of B/O elements and those of Ru elements partially overlap.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms B/O coordination with Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping of Ru_C - B - O /rGO show that the positions of B/O elements and those of Ru elements partially overlap.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES spectrum indicates Ru has typical metallic characteristics coincident with Ru foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES spectrum of Ru K edge indicated that the absorption edges of Ru_C - O /rGO, Ru_C - O/rGO, and Ru_C - B - O /rGO were highly coincident with the absorption edge of Ru foil, suggesting that Ru has typical metallic characteristics (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ru-B bond at 1.56 Å, Ru-O at 1.47 Å, Ru-B-O at 1.50 Å intermediate bond length.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-EXAFS spectrum of Ru_C - B /rGO and Ru_C - O /rGO indicates that the dominant peak was located at 1.56 and 1.47 Å, attributed to the bonding of Ru with B and O, respectively.

properties.technique: Fourier Transform Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure
properties.label: e

nodes.characterization_summary: SR-XRD patterns show rGO (002) peak near 11.71° and Ru (101) peak near 19.28°; negative peak shifts observed for Ru_C-B/rGO and Ru_C-B-O/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction (SR-XRD) patterns indicated that the Ru_C - B - O /rGO, Ru_C - B /rGO, and Ru_C - O /rGO catalysts exhibited two main peaks near 11.71° and 19.28°, respectively, corresponding to rGO (002) and Ru (101) crystal plane, as shown in Figure 2a.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS of Ru 3p shows Ru⁰ peak 0.4 eV negative shift in Ru_C-B/rGO vs Ru_C-B-O/rGO; B 1s shows B-Ru bond at 188 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS peak position of Ru⁰ in Ru_C - B /rGO exhibits a 0.4 eV negative shift relative to Ru_C - B - O /rGO ... The B 1s orbital analysis reveals that the B—Ru bond emerges at 188 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows significantly lower Ru content in Ru_C-B-O/G compared to other catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) tests indicate that the ratio of Ru in Ru_C - B - O / G was significantly lower compared with other catalysts (Table S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Quasi in-situ XPS shows Ru⁰ (461.1 eV) and Ruⁿ⁺ (462.5 eV) peak positions for Ru_C-B-O/rGO lie between those of Ru_C-O/rGO and Ru_C-B/rGO after electrochemical testing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, after electrochemical testing, the Ru⁰ (461.1 eV) and Ruⁿ⁺ (462.5 eV) peak positions of Ru_C-B-O/rGO were found to lie between those of Ru_C - O /rGO (Ru⁰ = 461.0 eV, Ruⁿ⁺ = 462.1 eV) and Ru_C - B /rGO (Ru⁰ = 461.4 eV, Ruⁿ⁺ = 463.9 eV).

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ infrared shows broad peak 3400-2800 cm⁻¹ for Ru_C-B-O/rGO indicating weakened hydrogen bond network and increased interfacial water migration rate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A broad peak was observed in the 3400 - 2800 cm⁻¹ region for Ru_C - B - O /rGO, suggesting that the coordination of B-O elements with Ru_C weakens the hydrogen bond network of interfacial water and increases its migration rate (Figure 5c).
